oom_killer.title: OOM killer killed {1}
oom_killer.detail: The kernel's out-of-memory killer terminated process "{1}" because the system ran out of available memory. Check what was consuming RAM around this time -- a runaway container, a large media scan, or a VM with too much allocated.

macvlan_crash.title: macvlan-related kernel call trace
macvlan_crash.detail: A kernel call trace was found referencing macvlan, the networking driver Docker's default bridge networking can rely on. This is a known-problematic combination on some kernels/NIC drivers -- switching custom networks to ipvlan often resolves it.

mce_hardware_error.title: Machine Check Exception -- hardware error
mce_hardware_error.detail: The CPU reported a Machine Check Exception hardware error. This is reported directly by the processor, not inferred -- it usually points to failing RAM, a CPU fault, or a power delivery problem. Worth investigating promptly.

edac_uncorrectable.title: EDAC uncorrectable memory error
edac_uncorrectable.detail: The memory controller's error detection and correction subsystem (EDAC) reported an uncorrectable error -- data corruption that ECC could not fix. Usually a failing DIMM.

btrfs_error.title: BTRFS error on {1}
btrfs_error.detail: The BTRFS filesystem driver reported an error on device "{1}". This can indicate filesystem corruption or an underlying disk problem -- a scrub is worth running.

xfs_error.title: XFS error on {1}
xfs_error.detail: The XFS filesystem driver reported internal corruption on "{1}". This can force the filesystem read-only to protect data -- worth running xfs_repair from a maintenance/safe mode boot.

ata_link_error.title: ATA link exception (SATA error)
ata_link_error.detail: An ATA/SATA link reported an exception mid-operation (not a normal boot-time link-up event). This usually points to a failing drive, cable, or backplane connector.

nic_link_flap.title: NIC {1} link down
nic_link_flap.detail: Network interface "{1}" reported its link going down. A single event during boot is normal; repeated flapping points to a bad cable, switch port, or failing NIC.

usb_disconnect.title: USB device disconnected
usb_disconnect.detail: A USB device was disconnected. If this is your Unraid boot flash drive or a USB-attached disk, an unexpected disconnect can cause array or docker instability.

kernel_call_trace.title: Kernel call trace
kernel_call_trace.detail: The kernel logged a call trace (a stack dump, usually from a warning, bug, or oops). Not fatal by itself, but worth reading the surrounding lines -- it's often the earliest sign of the actual problem (an OOM kill, a driver bug, or a hardware fault) before those show up as their own signatures.
